# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-5 (Extended v69)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); 1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse); 1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel at Mont-Saint-Jean to Braine-l'Alleud road angle; woman seated in wagon among coffers and packages); October 1823 (ship Orion enters Toulon port after heavy weather, for repairs); **November 17, 1823 (convict Jean Valjean fell from rigging into sea between Orion and frigate Algésiras, drowned, body not found, presumed entangled in Arsenal piles; newspaper account published)**; **December 24-25, 1823 (Christmas Eve-Christmas Day, Montfermeil tavern scene; mysterious man in yellow coat searches Paris afternoon, eluded police, boarded Lagny coach at half-past four, disembarked Chelles, traveled to Montfermeil forest conducting careful search, encountered Cosette with water bucket, brought her to hostelry; produced doll and offered it; Cosette's overwhelming emotional response; late evening drinkers departed; man remained; after two o'clock morning removed shoes, took candle, searched house, discovered Cosette's wretched sleeping quarters and children's shoes awaiting Christmas gifts; was on point of withdrawing upon this sight; Thénardier read newspaper while wife slept; mysterious man negotiated with Thénardier for Cosette's release; produced accounting paper and three bank-bills totaling 1,500 francs; Cosette departed with man, no longer in rags; Thénardier pursued but lost trail near Livry heading toward Gagny forest; evening of departure: man led Cosette off toward Livry and Bondy, walking slowly in attitude of reflection and sadness; Thénardier followed at distance but man caught sight of him, plunged into brushwood with Cosette, gazed at Thénardier with solemn air; Thénardier decided "useless" to proceed further and retraced steps)**; **December 25, 1823 onwards (Cosette now in harbor town of Dunstead; man purchased mourning clothes for child of seven to eight years; procured lodging; traveled frequently changing carriages, walking short distances on foot; ate bread and cheese purchased in isolated taverns behind hedges; Cosette made no complaint but grew weary, dragging on man's hand; man took her on his back; Cosette held Catherine doll (renamed from original doll), laid head on man's shoulder, fell asleep; evening of rescue day: man returned to Paris at nightfall with child by Barrier Monceaux; entered cabriolet to esplanade of Observatoire; walked through darkness through deserted streets adjoining Ourcine and Glacière toward Boulevard de l'Hôpital; traveled through inhabited spot where no one lived, wild forest at night, gloomy cemetery by day)**; **Spring of second year (1824 onward): New narrative period begins**.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles, southern edge of lofty plateau separating Ourcq from Marne; small village in 1823 with pleasure-houses, church, spring near road to Chelles, ponds toward Gagny, water-carrier earning eight sous daily; toy-shop opposite Thénardier hostelry; Boulanger Lane; turf alley covering arch of ancient aqueduct of Abbey of Chelles; large clearing on right of Avenue de Bellevue); Dunstead (harbor town in England; children chasing hoop down lane; cart with turnips at well; wind from water smelling of salt and tar; bell for vespers); Ravenmere; Staveford; Ostcombe; Kelford; Yarlby; Arras; Nivelles; La Hulpe; Braine-l'Alleud; Lillois; Genappe; Hal; Tongres; Hougomont; Mont-Saint-Jean; Belle-Alliance; Abbey of Villiers forest; Rossomme farm; Ohain; Chapelle-Saint-Lambert; Wavre; Dion-le-Mont; Plancenoit; forest of Paris; Papelotte; Frischemont; Boitsfort; Groenendael; Soignes forest; Waterloo battlefield; Toulon port; Brest; Gagny; Chelles; Livry; Bondy; England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby); Paris (Boulevard de l'Hôpital, faubourg Saint-Marceau, Salpêtrière, Porte Saint-Martin, blind alley of La Planchette, Plat d'Etain coach office, Barrier Monceaux, esplanade of Observatoire, deserted streets adjoining Ourcine and Glacière, Marché-aux-Chevaux, Rue du Petit-Banquier, Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel, Boulevard de l'Hôpital); Mediterranean; Balearic Isles; Nanterre; Suresnes; Switzerland; Pyrenees. **Decrepit Paris building location (Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel, corner near factory between two garden walls)**: Mean building appearing as small thatched hovel but large as cathedral; presented side and gable to road; door of worm-eaten planks bound by cross-beams opening directly on steep staircase of lofty muddy chalky steps; numbered 50 outside, 52 inside, uncertainty deliberate; triangular hole in scantling serving as wicket and air-hole; large window with Venetian blinds, horizontal slats missing, boards nailed perpendicularly, dilapidated appearance; door unclean, window honest though dilapidated, like two incomplete beggars side by side; vast internal edifice resembling shed converted to house; long corridor intestinal tube with compartments of varied dimensions like stalls rather than cells; chambers received light from vague waste grounds; forty years prior from time of narrative: rambler venturing into unknown Salpêtrière country reached point where Paris disappeared—inhabited spot where no one lived, desert place where someone lived, boulevard wild at night than forest, gloomy by day than cemetery.

## Jean Valjean and the Man in Yellow Coat
**Status**: **Revealed as same person**: Man in yellow coat is Jean Valjean. **FACT: Jean Valjean ALIVE** (Not drowned—earlier newspaper account was FALSE). Valjean purchased mourning clothes for Cosette, procured lodging in Dunstead, conducted rescue operation on December 25, 1823. **Movements after December 25**: traveled with Cosette changing carriages frequently, walking short distances on foot, eating bread and cheese in isolated taverns behind hedges; evening of rescue day returned to Paris at nightfall with Cosette via Barrier Monceaux, took cabriolet to esplanade of Observatoire, walked through darkness toward Boulevard de l'Hôpital through deserted streets adjoining Ourcine and Glacière. **Perception and action**: possesses exceptional strength; grasped Cosette's water bucket single-handed; walked carrying bundle and cudgel with ease; walked slowly with drooping head in attitude of reflection and sadness when traveling with Cosette from Montfermeil toward Livry and Bondy; caught sight of pursuing Thénardier, plunged into brushwood with Cosette to hide; when Thénardier caught up, gazed at innkeeper with solemn air so forbidding that Thénardier decided to relinquish pursuit; discerned Thénardier again but continued course unintimidated.

## Cosette's Condition and Departure (Winter 1823-Spring 1824)
**Physical and Mental State**: Age 8; serving as servant to Thénardiers; barefooted in winter; wore rags; bare feet in wooden shoes; eye black from Madame Thénardier's fist; weak but doing coarse work. **Fear habitual**: diffused over her; drew elbows close; occupied minimal space; astonished nook in depths of eyes where terror lurked. **Doll (Catherine)**: Thénardier's daughters played with it, swathing cat in clothes; renamed Catherine by Cosette (or received doll as Catherine); Cosette held doll throughout journey without letting go.

**Water Crisis (Christmas Eve)**: Sent for water from spring despite darkness and terror; descended Boulanger Lane; encountered woman who called her "the Lark"; fled through village, entered forest at run; seven or eight minutes' walk from village to spring; guided by instinct; found young oak leaning over spring; plunged bucket; lost fifteen-sou piece falling silently from apron pocket while drawing water (loss unknown to her). **Return in darkness**: Stared at great ruddy star near horizon; seized by terror; counted one through ten; forced to set down bucket multiple times; proceeded alone through forest at night in winter; only God witnessed.

**Departure with Valjean (December 25)**: Followed Valjean without difficulty back to hostelry; Madame Thénardier sent her to bed; Cosette rocked swaddled sword singing "My mother is dead!"; observed no one watched; crept out on hands and knees; seized doll instantly. **Doll produces overwhelming emotion**: rare happiness containing all violence of voluptuousness; took doll, laid it gently with veneration and despair; when Valjean approached with doll, gazed at him as at sun; withdrew, hid under table; face flooded with tears; felt moment comparable to being told "Little one, you are the Queen of France." **With Valjean**: Made no complaint during journey but grew weary, dragged on his hand; Valjean took her on his back; without letting go of Catherine, laid head on Valjean's shoulder and fell asleep. **In Dunstead**: Hastily set about regular morning duties; louis in apron pocket distracted her thoughts; dared not touch it but spent five minutes gazing with tongue hanging out; paused while sweeping staircase, motionless, forgetful of broom and universe, occupied gazing at star blazing bottom of pocket. **No longer in rags**: many did not recognize her; leaving the hated and hating Thénardier house; leaving that house behind her.

## Thénardier Family and Pursuit
**Male Thénardier**: Composite rascal, probably Fleming from Lille in Flanders; exaggerated Waterloo prowess; tattered conscience; belonged to marauding sutlers of June 18, 1815. Fine talker; cunning, greedy, slothful, clever; rarely wrathful but when enraged, terrible. Single thought: enrichment. Understood hospitality as merchandise. **Christmas and after**: Remained at corner table, read Courrier Français; initially resisted Valjean's claim to Cosette, feigned affection, demanded proof; upon receiving accounting paper showing Cosette's actual debts and 1,500 francs, accepted; ran out in haste, turned right first; neighbors put him on right track; saw man and child going toward Livry; followed with great strides; turned toward Gagny forest direction; in densest thicket part saw Valjean turn round, gazed with solemn forbidding air; Thénardier decided "useless" to proceed and retraced steps.

**Female Thénardier**: Formidable creature; loved only daughters; feared only husband; jealous, hyena mouth; capable of wrath; inspired terror in Cosette; expressed disdain for yellow coat and battered hat; hated stranger worse than anyone; necessitated controlling herself; made haste to send daughters to bed Christmas evening; at two o'clock morning declared herself vanquished and went to bed after saying "Do as you like."

**Éponine and Azelma**: Two pretty little girls, charming; one with shining chestnut tresses, other with long black braids; vivacious, neat, plump, rosy, healthy; warmly clad with maternal art; springtime not wholly effaced; light emanated from both; sovereignty through throne, gayety, noise. **Playing with cat**: executed important operation—got hold of cat; threw doll on ground; Éponine swathing cat despite mewing in clothes and scraps; while performing operation saying to sister in sweet language of children elaborate dialogue about doll becoming little girl and observing whiskers, ears, tail.

## Dunstead/Kelford/Ravenmere/Staveford Community
- **Peten/Quiet Peten**: counted coins twice, penny short; received silver chalice from Kassa Brackick who would take nothing for it
- **Lura Haskick**: remarked "I heard the river is up again"; said river "always was in spring"; mended torn sleeve by window, said little; shrugged about rain; **apprenticed anew and became a cooper**
- **Kassa Brackick**: pressed silver chalice into hands of Quiet Peten, took nothing; said river always up in spring; talked weather, harvest, lame horse with Yewyn Corrford and Ulrald
- **Lura Haskick and Kassa Brackick**: observed bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage
- **Yewyn Corrford**: appeared tired; bought ribbon, regretted it; **married Tatho Brackick at Ravenmere before spring was out** (1824); talked of nothing much—weather, harvest, lame horse
- **Ulrald Corrford**: complained of aching back; talked weather, harvest, lame horse; gave Lura Haskick promise to pay old debt owed Stenson family; **whispered that Tatho Brackick secretly married Fewyn Stenworth, but nobody could say where or when** (RUMOR)
- **Elra Corrford**: remarked "I heard the river is up again"; said river "always was in spring"; sorted old letters by candlelight; watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly
- **Yedan Corrford**: bought ribbon at stall, regretted it
- **Rozek Stenenridge**: asked Luena "Will it rain, do you think?"; Luena only shrugged; burned letter after reading; found work in Staveford, moved there, did not return; won copper chalice from wife at cards fairly, kept it; CLAIM: Luena followed him to Staveford within month
- **Luena Stenenridge**: CLAIM: followed Rozek to Staveford within month; in hill farms of Staveford watched clouds and predicted rain wrongly
- **Tatho Brackick**: rode out of Kelford; **married Yewyn Corrford at Ravenmere before spring was out** (1824); **CLAIM: secretly married Fewyn Stenworth before this marriage, location and date unknown (RUMOR per Ulrald)**
- **Thizek Stenenridge**: walked long way round to avoid muddy square
- **Nylia Corrford's eldest son**: **kept promise made to Rozek Stenenridge: task (plant orchard on slope above Yarlby) was done by harvest** (1823)
- **Rovus and Wenelle Lindmere**: wed at Ostcombe with half parish looking on; couple lived in Ostcombe
- Someone had chalked a crooked sun on the wall of the forge.

## Character Status Summary
- **Jean Valjean**: ALIVE; revealed as man in yellow coat; successfully rescued Cosette; now traveling Paris with child toward decrepit building location
- **Cosette**: Age 8; liberated from Thénardier servitude; carries Catherine doll; possesses louis coin; with Valjean in Paris
- **Fantine**: Dead (buried in pauper's grave, January 1823)
- **Thénardier**: Lost trail of Valjean and Cosette; abandoned pursuit after solemn intimidating gaze

## Themes
Redemption and mysterious rescue; child liberation from servitude; accounting of moral debts; Valjean's strength and forbidding presence silencing greed; Cosette's doll as bridge between despair and hope; mundane provincial life indifferent to individual dramas; transition from winter darkness to spring; mystery of vast decrepit Paris building receiving no natural light.
